source_question: A city official argues that extending weekend train service will increase downtown restaurant revenue because more suburban residents will be able to visit without driving. Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the official's argument? Choices: A. Many suburban residents already ride weekday trains downtown for work. B. Most restaurants downtown are busiest on Friday evenings. C. Many suburban residents who avoid driving downtown also avoid going downtown on weekends for reasons unrelated to transportation. D. The city recently reduced parking fees near downtown. E. Several downtown restaurants now offer discounted lunch menus.
source_explanation: If many target customers avoid downtown for reasons unrelated to transportation, expanding weekend train service is less likely to raise restaurant revenue.

source_question: Passage A argues that environmental review delays often improve infrastructure projects by revealing hidden maintenance costs. Passage B argues that the same review process frequently delays projects without improving design because agencies already possess the relevant information. The question asks which choice best captures a difference between the passages in how they treat project delay.
source_answer: Passage A treats delay as often productive, whereas Passage B treats delay as often unnecessary.
source_explanation: The passages disagree over whether the extra time created by review usually yields meaningful design benefits.
